newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-OPINION - Inside Canberra - Red tape stalemate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-OPINION - Inside Canberra - Red tape stalemate.

text.p: Essentially the government has failed what small business regarded as an election promise -- to cut the level of red tape by 50 percent in its first term in office.

Ah, says the Small Business Minister, Geoff Prosser, that was not the promise -- the promise was to appoint a task force within six months of coming to office to make recommendations to the government on revenue neutral measures to reduce the paper and compliance burden on small business by 50 per cent.

Well, it could be said to have failed here as well because, as was apparent to anyone with basic knowledge of the working of the bureaucracy, the task force could not make recommendations for such a cut on the basis of revenue neutrality, as it was instructed to do by the terms of reference.
Instead it has proposed a raft of taxation reforms relating to the wholesale sales tax, fringe benefits tax, provisional tax and payroll tax which are not revenue neutral.
But, says the task force, changes are necessary in these areas to relieve the regulatory burden on small business.

Maybe, but if we are going to have tax reform, let's have a fair dinkum across-the-board-reform of the whole system (including vertical imbalance about which the states complain) and not just reforms based on what small business is whingeing about.
Nothing concrete has been suggested by the task force to attack the biggest problem -- by far the greatest volume of red tape is generated by the states and local government.
There will be talks etc in the Council of Australian Government, but that is all -- talks.
This whole red tape issue has been really overblown, built up by Prime Minister John Howard as virtually the central problem facing small business.
You can get small business people to whinge about almost everything (Your editor is a noted small business whinger). But it really was not such a big deal for them.
(Views here are those of Inside Canberra, not Reuters)
